title: Silergy’s 2026 PMIC and Digital Audio Updates Point to Denser Power and Audio Integration
dek: Silergy’s Q2 2026 catalogue updates include multi-output power-management and digital-audio devices that can reduce supporting-component complexity around increasingly intelligent electronics.
summary: Edge-AI products still depend on less glamorous supporting silicon. Silergy’s updates show how PMIC and audio integration can change board area, thermal margin and BOM complexity around the main processor.
whyItMatters: Power rails and audio are supporting subsystems, but they often determine board area, thermal margin and BOM complexity.
Production-stage devices with evaluation boards can be more immediately useful to product teams than early AI-silicon announcements.
Automotive-grade features should not be assumed to translate directly into consumer fit; voltage, cost and qualification still need product-specific review.

reporting.heading: AI products still live or die on supporting silicon
paragraphs: Edge-AI systems attract attention for processors and NPUs, but the surrounding power and audio architecture remains a major source of board complexity. Silergy’s Q2 2026 catalogue updates show continued integration in those less visible layers.
The SA47301 family brings multiple power outputs into a managed PMIC architecture, while the SY24145 family provides digital audio amplification with DSP-oriented functions in production-stage parts.

reporting.heading: Integration can free board area and engineering time
paragraphs: Fewer discrete regulators and a more integrated audio path can simplify layout, validation and firmware control in devices with several voltage rails or compact speaker systems.
That can matter in smart appliances, voice terminals and other connected products, even when the parts themselves are not marketed as AI devices.

reporting.heading: Availability matters more than headline novelty
paragraphs: Silergy’s product pages identify production status and evaluation-board support for relevant audio devices. That makes the signal useful from a sourcing perspective, but exact pricing, lead times and product-grade suitability still need confirmation.
FlyPig will treat these parts as enabling components to be matched after the main compute and product power budget are defined.

flypigTake: Silergy illustrates why a Taiwan technology graph cannot stop at processors. Power and audio ICs can materially change board area, thermal design and BOM complexity, but they should be evaluated as part of a complete product architecture.
sourceName: Silergy official product pages and Q2 2026 catalogue
